evidenceRecords.text: Defense autonomy startup Rownd has secured a $10 million contract with the Department of War as it develops low-cost, autonomous drones designed for military operations.
The company is also expanding its operations in Wisconsin and North Carolina, adding jobs and investing in drone research and development.
Headquartered in Raleigh, NC, Rownd is focused on what the defense industry calls attritable mass: deploying drones that are affordable enough to be replaced if lost in combat.
The approach aims to give military forces more autonomous systems without relying on expensive platforms that are difficult to replace.
Rownd’s technology is designed to let drones process information and make decisions onboard rather than depend on constant cloud connectivity or centralized ground control.
Its AI software also enables drones to communicate and coordinate with one another, including when a swarm loses its connection to external networks.
The company recently put those capabilities to the test during a three-day exercise with Air Force personnel in Alabama.
Rownd’s quadcopters completed 41 flights, including four mobile flights and four fleet tests using onboard AI.
The exercise also marked the company’s first drone swarm demonstration, with up to three aircraft flying simultaneously.
Rownd used the exercise to demonstrate another part of its development process: improving its AI models using real-world flight data.
Each night, the team retrained the drones’ computer-vision models using data collected during the day’s flights and uploaded the updated models before the next day’s missions.
According to the company, this process significantly improved accuracy.

items.title: AI agents develop their own 'artificial natural language' to communicate about complex data
items.originalTitle: AI agents develop their own 'artificial natural language' to communicate about complex data
items.summary: Jérôme Botoko Ekila, a doctoral student at the VUB's AI Lab, explains, "Instead of forcing AI systems to communicate in a human language that does not correspond to their sensors, we allow them to develop their own 'artificial natural language.' They construct effective concepts that correspond exactly to what they perceive via their sensors, even if the data is incomprehensible to humans." Because sensors on different machines or vehicles can never be calibrated identically in practice, the researchers believe that this language offers the ideal solution.

evidenceRecords.text: Jérôme Botoko Ekila, a doctoral student at the VUB's AI Lab, explains, "Instead of forcing AI systems to communicate in a human language that does not correspond to their sensors, we allow them to develop their own 'artificial natural language.' They construct effective concepts that correspond exactly to what they perceive via their sensors, even if the data is incomprehensible to humans."
Because sensors on different machines or vehicles can never be calibrated identically in practice, the researchers believe that this language offers the ideal solution.

Paul Van Eecke, a professor of artificial intelligence at the VUB, says, "In industrial or physical applications, it is simply unrealistic to expect all the sensors on different robots or vehicles to be calibrated in exactly the same way.
"Humans solve this problem through language: if I say I am standing near the 'red car,' we understand each other without our eyes registering exactly the same color values.
Language provides a layer of abstraction above the sensor readings, and this is precisely what we are now allowing these AI agents to construct autonomously."

Instead of preprogrammed words or fixed codes, the researchers provided the agents with the basic mechanisms underpinning the evolution of human language: the local invention of words, the adaptation of conceptual prototypes and the incorporation of feedback following successful or failed communication.
Katrien Beuls, a professor at UNamur, explains, "What's fascinating is that there's no central computer imposing the rules.
Each time, we let two agents communicate with one another at a local level.
It is solely through these individual interactions and updates that a global convention emerges spontaneously across the entire population.
The universal applicability of the method has been demonstrated across 37 varied and complex data sets.
The agents successfully developed their own vocabulary to communicate, notably regarding physicochemical analyses of wine, NASA data on exoplanets, visual data sets and images of birds or faces.
In all these situations, the agents successfully synthesized the data into new, shared concepts.

Agility Robotics Inc. today said it is working with Nyobolt on a fast-recharge battery system for its Digit 5 system.
The technology will allow the robot to work more than 20 hours in a day, the companies claimed.
“For our customers, Digit’s uptime is the business case,” stated Daniel Diez, chief business officer at Agility.
“Digit 5 will deliver more than 20 hours of productive work in a 24-hour day, more than two full shifts.
That’s the kind of gain that materially improves the value customers get from Digit and the economics of deploying a humanoid robot fleet.

Nyobolt’s ultra-fast charging technology gets us there, and it’s one of the pieces that makes Digit 5 ready for full-scale operation.” Founded in 2015, Agility said Digit is “the first multi-purpose, human-centric robot that is ‘Made for Work’ and commercially deployed today.” The Salem, Ore.-based company said it has accumulated more than 65,000 of real-world operations .
Last month, it released Digit 5 with new legs and acknowledged that it is considering wheeled locomotion.

In May 2026, the company achieved a $1 billion valuation by raising $60 million including support from Symbotic Inc. “Nyobolt’s technology was chosen because Digit 5 will need more power from a smaller, lighter pack in environments where reliability isn’t optional,” said Sai Shivareddy, co-founder and CEO of Nyobolt.

“Agility set an exceptionally high bar for what a battery has to withstand in live warehouse and manufacturing environments, and this partnership shows what’s possible when ultra-fast charging is engineered for the toughest conditions in physical AI.” Digit 5 features longer runtime for humanoid customers Agility described Digit 5 as its first humanoid robot designed to work in close proximity to people safely and at scale.
The company asserted that this will let Digit 5 customers target longer operating windows, more productive shifts, and more demanding task sequences.

evidenceRecords.text: The article Anthropic's Q3 revenue hits $16.8B but growth slows ahead of planned November IPO appeared first on The Decoder .
Slowing growth and a tough market are hurting Anthropic's valuation ahead of its planned November IPO.
Anthropic shared its quarterly numbers with potential investors at a private meeting in San Francisco, according to multiple US media reports.
Third-quarter revenue hit $16.8 billion.
That marks a roughly 45 percent jump from the second quarter and is more than 3.6 times the company's total annual revenue for 2025.
Growth has slowed, though.
In the second quarter, surging demand for the developer tool Claude Code had pushed revenue up by more than 140 percent compared to Q1.
Anthropic is far from that pace now, though a summer slowdown is one likely factor since people typically work less during those months and burn through fewer tokens.
OpenAI also launched a strong competitor with Astra in September, which Anthropic only successfully countered in late September with Opus 5.5.
The Financial Times reports this was the second straight quarter of adjusted profitability for the AI lab.
The company is cash-flow positive, too.
During the third quarter, Anthropic generated $1.70 in revenue for every dollar it spent on compute.
Anthropic also estimates that 5 to 7 percent of its revenue comes from distillation.

items.summary: Now, Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle is attempting to do something about it. Telle announced Monday at the Association of the U.S. Army’s annual meeting the creation of an enterprise-level Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning Task Force focused on soldiers’ quality of life. The task force includes leaders from facility operations, contracting and military engineering who can “cut through bureaucratic silos,” the Army said in a Monday statement .

evidenceRecords.text: Now, Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle is attempting to do something about it.

Telle announced Monday at the Association of the U.S. Army’s annual meeting the creation of an enterprise-level Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning Task Force focused on soldiers’ quality of life.
The task force includes leaders from facility operations, contracting and military engineering who can “cut through bureaucratic silos,” the Army said in a Monday statement .
The announcement follows a directive from Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth last year to create another military-wide task force to improve barracks .
“Secretary of War Hegseth has said every service member deserves clean, comfortable, and safe housing,” Telle said at the annual meeting in Washington, D.C.

“This has never been done before — we’re taking this for the first time to the national level, to deliver results across the country to soldiers.” Jordan Gillis, assistant secretary of the Army for installations, energy and environment, said in a statement that HVAC is the top quality-of-life complaint that leadership hears from soldiers.

The Government Accountability Office reported in August that the Defense Department does not request enough funding to fully meet its installation maintenance and major improvement needs, leading to a backlog of deferred maintenance at barracks.
Hundreds of thousands of service members live in military barracks, with concerns about poor living conditions and management going back decades, according to the government watchdog.
Before the end of the fiscal year in September, the Army directed $15 million toward 44 high-priority HVAC projects across multiple installations, the service said in a statement.

“While that effort brought immediate relief to specific facilities, the [task force] leaders recognized that one-time emergency funding cannot replace a comprehensive, proactive strategy,” the Army said.
Members of the task force will work directly with garrison commanders to find HVAC projects for 2027 and 2028, the Army said.

The article Nvidia's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is an open model built to run enterprise AI agents nonstop appeared first on The Decoder .
Nvidia has released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open multimodal model with 120 billion parameters built for agent tasks and document analysis in enterprise settings.
Nvidia has released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open multimodal model with 120 billion parameters built for enterprise agents.
Two compact Bolt models designed to bring AI agents to local PCs and edge devices are launching alongside it.
Nvidia built Nemotron 3.5 Super VL for specialized agents that run continuously in the background, processing text, images, documents, and videos.
Two smaller models for local hardware ship at the same time.
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB runs agent tasks on local machines, while the smaller Bolt E4B 4GB targets fast voice assistants and will follow later this month.
Both models offer the "highest intelligence per gigabyte of memory," Nvidia claims.
On a single GPU, Super VL delivers up to five times the throughput of other open models of similar size on agent tasks, according to Nvidia, citing the Artificial Analysis leaderboard.
In an independent test by EXO Labs on the DGX Spark, no other model was both more accurate and faster.
That speed advantage pays off when agents need to grind through large task volumes over days or weeks.
Against closed frontier models, Nvidia is pitching Super VL to companies that want to fine-tune with their own data and run the model on their own servers, free from a provider's terms of service.
Nvidia says that could appeal to an insurer that continuously screens claims for fraud, or a financial services firm that scores creditworthiness by its own criteria.
Weights are available on Hugging Face for Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B-A12B and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB.

items.summary: Insider Brief Researchers from Argonne National Laboratory and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign demonstrated a hybrid system that couples magnetic spin waves with superconducting circuits for quantum information processing. The experiment showed that information carried by spin waves in a thin magnetic film can transfer into microwave signals in a superconducting circuit, with the hybrid mode supporting one-way propagation.

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief Researchers from Argonne National Laboratory and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign demonstrated a hybrid system that couples magnetic spin waves with superconducting circuits for quantum information processing.

The experiment showed that information carried by spin waves in a thin magnetic film can transfer into microwave signals in a superconducting circuit, with the hybrid mode supporting one-way propagation.
The approach could support compact, on-chip quantum systems by combining spin-wave devices with superconducting circuit technology to help control signal direction and reduce unwanted feedback.
PRESS RELEASE — Quantum information systems could one day shape everyday life through faster computing and more secure communication.

A new result from the U.S. Department of Energy’s Argonne National Laboratory and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign marks an important step for magnetic spins — a quantum property of matter that can be used to store and manipulate information — to play a role in the future of quantum information processing.
The researchers show that the ripples in the magnetic state of a material, called spin waves, can interact with superconducting circuits, tiny circuits that can carry microwave signals.
The result is a hybrid system in which these two different ways of carrying information can work together.
Superconducting circuits, standard parts of many quantum information systems, help connect and control signals inside those systems.
They send and receive microwave signals in a way that strengthens communication with other parts of the device.
Spin waves offer a different advantage.
Under certain conditions, spin waves are unidirectional, meaning they naturally prefer one direction of travel over the opposite.
That is useful because quantum systems often need one-way signal control to help prevent unwanted noise from leaking back into the quantum components.

items.originalTitle: Strengthening Advanced-Node Interconnects Through Automated Via Insertion
items.summary: To understand the need for automated via optimization, first consider the physical challenges at play. In a typical advanced-node interconnect, the resistance of a single via can be significantly higher than that of a corresponding length of metal wire. As current flows through these narrow vertical structures, the resulting heat and atomic displacement can lead to electromigration – the gradual movement of metal atoms that eventually creates voids or shorts. Historically, designers mitigated these risks by manually adding redundant vias to critical signal paths and power grids.

evidenceRecords.text: 1: The increasing complexity of advanced-node layouts requires automated solutions to identify valid locations for redundant via insertion without violating foundry rules.
To understand the need for automated via optimization, first consider the physical challenges at play.
In a typical advanced-node interconnect, the resistance of a single via can be significantly higher than that of a corresponding length of metal wire.

As current flows through these narrow vertical structures, the resulting heat and atomic displacement can lead to electromigration – the gradual movement of metal atoms that eventually creates voids or shorts.
Historically, designers mitigated these risks by manually adding redundant vias to critical signal paths and power grids.
The redundant vias provide parallel paths for current, lowering the effective resistance and reducing the current density through any single via.
However, at 5nm and below, the sheer density of the layout and the complexity of foundry design rules make manual insertion practically impossible.
Figure 1 illustrates the problem.
Fig. 1: The increasing complexity of advanced-node layouts requires automated solutions to identify valid locations for redundant via insertion without violating foundry rules.
The technical benefits of automated via insertion are most evident in the power delivery network.
In high-performance SoCs, the PDN must deliver massive amounts of current with minimal voltage drop.
As the number of metal layers increases, the vertical resistance through the via stacks becomes a dominant contributor to the total IR drop.
From an EM perspective, additional vias provide a critical safety net.

Electromigration is a statistical phenomenon; while a single via might be designed to handle a specific current, manufacturing variations can lead to localized “hot spots” where the current density exceeds the safe limit.
By providing parallel paths, automated insertion ensures that the current is distributed more evenly, reducing the likelihood of a catastrophic failure over the lifetime of the device.
Automated via insertion is a prime example of how this shift-left methodology can provide tangible benefits in terms of silicon reliability and schedule predictability.

State officials say they are receiving fewer election-specific federal briefings than in previous cycles, while others who track foreign influence have observed routine exchanges with government and technology companies fall away.

evidenceRecords.text: The Trump administration’s retreat from programs that track foreign influence operations has weakened various cross-sector relationships used to identify and confront those campaigns as midterm elections fast approach — even as artificial intelligence makes those operations easier to deploy — multiple sources told Nextgov/FCW .

State officials say they are receiving fewer election-specific federal briefings than in previous cycles, while others who track foreign influence have observed routine exchanges with government and technology companies fall away.
Some also note that federal workforce departures have weakened cooperation with outside partners, including social media platforms, to track false information online.

While the federal government continues to gather intelligence on foreign threats to U.S. elections, some of those who lean on those findings say federal agencies are less reliably sharing information with non-federal researchers and state officials responsible for countering those campaigns.
That cooperation began to weaken before President Donald Trump returned to office, and his administration has since dismantled several programs dedicated to countering the problem.
This story is based on interviews with current and former federal officials, state election officials and specialists in cybersecurity and influence operations.

Their concerns come as fast-evolving AI tools now allow foreign influence operators to do more than just generate fake images or audio, instead helping them produce plausible-sounding messages, find audiences to target and autonomously adjust campaigns at a scale not seen before.
The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency referred questions about foreign malign influence to the Justice Department, saying that influence operations fall outside CISA’s mission.
“Election security is national security, and protecting our critical infrastructure remains a top priority for the Trump Administration, DHS, and CISA,” a CISA spokesperson said.
Foreign influence operations aim to shape what people believe and how they act, often without revealing who is behind the message.

evidenceRecords.text: It is the "backbone of military communications in Ukraine" that provides vital high-speed internet to forces across the country.
Starlink satellites operated by Elon Musk's SpaceX provide high-speed internet - something modern war relies heavily on.
For Ukraine, it is vital for communications on the battlefield and effective drone warfare.
But on Tuesday night, Starlink suddenly and unexpectedly restricted the speed at which drones could fly while still maintaining internet connection.
This disrupted some battlefield "missions", a top Ukrainian official said, and hampered Kyiv's ability to protect itself from incoming Russian attacks.

"Starlink gives Ukraine the ability to see what's coming, to protect people," Kurt Volker, former US ambassador to Nato, told the BBC's Radio 4 Today programme. "If you cut that off, then more people are going to get killed - and that is a very cynical and callous decision to slow that down the way that has been done."
The move has once again shown how Starlink can impact the conflict, which has been raging since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Starlink is an internet network that uses satellites in low Earth orbit to provide connectivity, particularly in remote areas and battlefields.
The US government has allowed Ukraine to use Starlink and Starshield in its defence against Russia.
Musk cut Moscow's access to the service in February, giving Kyiv an advantage in the conflict.

Put simply, Starlink uses its thousands of satellites to ping high-speed internet back to almost every corner of the globe, using terminals on the ground that users can easily buy and set up themselves.
As Musk said, they have two instructions: "point at sky, plug in".
In Ukraine, both Starlink (the civilian service) and Starshield (the military service) are used, depending on what communications are needed.
"Starlink gives Ukraine the ability to see what's coming, to protect people," Kurt Volker, former US ambassador to Nato, told the BBC's Radio 4 Today programme.
Because Russia is not authorised to use Starlink, when Ukraine sends long-range missiles deep into Russia to hit oil refineries, the network does not work.

items.title: FirstQFM Model Cuts Single-Qubit Gate Times by 33% on QuantWare Processor
items.originalTitle: FirstQFM Model Cuts Single-Qubit Gate Times by 33% on QuantWare Processor
items.summary: Insider Brief FirstQFM applied its quantum foundation model to a 21-qubit QuantWare superconducting processor at the Israeli Quantum Computing Center, reducing single-qubit gate execution time by 33% without reducing gate fidelity. The model generated custom pulse-level gate implementations from existing calibration data and identified five qubit pairs with improved Bell-state fidelity, with the improvements confirmed in independent hardware runs.

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief FirstQFM applied its quantum foundation model to a 21-qubit QuantWare superconducting processor at the Israeli Quantum Computing Center, reducing single-qubit gate execution time by 33% without reducing gate fidelity.

The model generated custom pulse-level gate implementations from existing calibration data and identified five qubit pairs with improved Bell-state fidelity, with the improvements confirmed in independent hardware runs.

The work used Quantum Machines’ control and calibration infrastructure alongside NVIDIA accelerated computing, and FirstQFM plans to expand its optimizations as QuantWare develops larger quantum processors.
PRESS RELEASE — FirstQFM today announced results from applying FirstQFM’s quantum foundation model to a QuantWare superconducting quantum processor at the Israeli Quantum Computing Center (IQCC).
FirstQFM ’s foundation model builds on top of Quantum Machines’ native calibration stack, and generated single-qubit gates that reduced execution time by 33% on a QuantWare Contralto-D21 QPU.
Gates were validated directly on the QuantWare processor using randomized benchmarking with no loss of gate fidelity.
The model generated custom pulse-level implementations of gates from calibration data produced by the Quantum Machines’ calibration stack with no additional quantum hardware measurements required.
This shifts more of the gate optimization process from scarce QPU time to classical compute.
The model also identified improvements to two-qubit gates, which are central to entanglement and typically more challenging to calibrate than single-qubit operations.

Using existing calibration data together with a short hardware probe, the model identified five qubit pairs with higher Bell-state fidelity with each improvement confirmed in independent hardware runs.

FirstQFM developed its foundation model using NVIDIA accelerated computing hardware and software, including the Leonardo supercomputer and the NVIDIA CUDA-Q open source hybrid platform, before fine-tuning and applying the model to the QuantWare processor.

“On QuantWare ’s processor, our model was able to use existing calibration data to generate shorter single-qubit gates while preserving fidelity, and to improve selected two-qubit operations.” As superconducting quantum processors grow, calibration becomes a harder control problem.

items.title: Using electronic structure to guide AI in designing new materials
items.originalTitle: Using electronic structure to guide AI in designing new materials
items.summary: Structure dictates function. Scientists are increasingly using artificial intelligence (AI) to design the arrangement of atoms in new materials with desired properties. Now, researchers at the Institute of Industrial Science, The University of Tokyo, have extended a leading generative AI model so that it designs the electronic structure of a material together with its crystal structure. The new model, named MatterGen-e⁻, is reported in npj Computational Materials.

evidenceRecords.text: Structure dictates function.
Scientists are increasingly using artificial intelligence (AI) to design the arrangement of atoms in new materials with desired properties.

Now, researchers at the Institute of Industrial Science, The University of Tokyo, have extended a leading generative AI model so that it designs the electronic structure of a material together with its crystal structure.
The new model, named MatterGen-e⁻, is reported in npj Computational Materials.

New materials have traditionally been invented using trial-and-error experiments (a slow process) or randomly generating candidates on a computer and screening the results (which is computationally expensive).

A game changer is inverse design—a target property is specified initially (e.g., the specific band gap or formation energy), and AI rapidly and directly designs a matching structure for a stable crystal.
Generative machine learning models, which learn from existing crystal data, are well suited to this task because they can create entirely new materials.

The chemical and physical properties of a crystalline material (e.g., the hardness, electrical conductivity and optical behavior) depend on atomic-scale properties: the crystal structure (the arrangement of molecules in a repeating three-dimensional pattern) and the electronic structure (how electrons are distributed among energy levels and around atoms).
For target values of the formation energy and band gap, MatterGen-e⁻ produced substantially more structures that were simultaneously valid, stable, unique and novel than MatterGen.

By outputting electronic descriptors together with each structure, MatterGen-e⁻ also provides the density of states of newly generated materials, which agreed reasonably well with first-principles calculations.

These findings point to a design principle for generative models in materials science: using physically meaningful intermediate representations, such as electronic structure, rather than atomic structure alone.
Using electronic structure to guide AI in designing new materials (2026, October 15)

Thursday, Oct. 29 During U.S. spacewalk 100, NASA astronaut Anil Menon and CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk will exit the station’s Quest airlock to install and deploy an International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (IROSA) on the 2A electrical power channel.
The solar array will be the seventh IROSA and will provide additional power to support critical station operations, including its safe and controlled deorbit.
Thursday, Nov. 5 During U.S. spacewalk 101, Menon and Kutryk will install and deploy the eighth and final IROSA on the 3B channel of the space station, completing the power augmentation upgrades.
The final two roll-out solar arrays will complete the space station’s power system augmentation.
Together, the eight roll-out arrays will increase available power by up to 30%, boosting the station’s electric power generation capacity from 160 kilowatts to approximately 215 kilowatts.
NASA will share additional coverage details about U.S. spacewalks 100 and 101 closer to each operation on the agency’s live events web page and the space station blog .
The spacewalks will be the 285th and 286th conducted in support of space station assembly, maintenance, and upgrades.

items.title: Why are eight US states suing OpenAI?
items.originalTitle: Why are eight US states suing OpenAI?
items.summary: Eight US states have filed the most significant coordinated state action against tech giant OpenAI, adding to a wave of legal challenges that the firm is facing as it prepares for a public listing. Recent legal and regulatory challenges have highlighted concerns about how AI chatbots and social media platforms are used and triggered discussions on policies for identifying and addressing user conversations that threaten violence.

evidenceRecords.text: Eight US states have filed the most significant coordinated state action against tech giant OpenAI, adding to a wave of legal challenges that the firm is facing as it prepares for a public listing.

Recent legal and regulatory challenges have highlighted concerns about how AI chatbots and social media platforms are used and triggered discussions on policies for identifying and addressing user conversations that threaten violence.
On Wednesday, attorneys general from eight states – Iowa, Kansas, Arizona, Arkansas, Idaho, Montana, Nebraska and West ⁠Virginia – said they had also sued OpenAI in courts across the country.

Additionally, the suits accuse OpenAI of violating state consumer protection laws by misleading users about ‌the ⁠safety of their AI tool, which in fact poses a danger to the health of the states’ residents.

The states are seeking orders forcing OpenAI to make substantial changes to how ChatGPT works, as well as measures barring the company ⁠from developing AI models that can improve themselves until it can ensure those models are aligned with human values.

The province of British Columbia filed a lawsuit against OpenAI in a California court in September, seven months after 18-year-old Jesse Van Rootselaar shot eight people in the small Canadian town of Tumbler Ridge, including his mother and half-brother, before dying by suicide.
The lawsuit alleges that OpenAI had failed to notify authorities about concerning user interactions on ChatGPT, accusing the company of “aiding and abetting a mass shooting”.

OpenAI said it had flagged a ChatGPT account linked to Van Rootselaar for abuse eight months before the shooting, and deactivated it, but did not alert police at the time because the user’s content “did not meet the higher threshold required for referral” – meaning the company did not believe it indicated a credible, imminent risk of a plan for violent acts.

evidenceRecords.text: Accelerating the search for novel antimicrobial peptides using Google Antigravity for Science.
New antibiotics are urgently needed to help with rising levels of antimicrobial resistance, but searching for new therapeutics is often a slow, labor-intensive process.
With Google Antigravity, our agentic development platform, this process can now be made easier.

Google Antigravity provides an agentic science workbench that empowers biologists to discover, structurally evaluate, and prioritize promising targets quickly, compressing what used to be a fragmented search over multiple databases into a single session.
It also helps researchers scan through millions of previously uncharacterized proteins in the UniProt database using ProtNLM, a model that predicts biological function from amino acid sequences.

This technical walkthrough shows how biologists used Google Antigravity to uncover a novel antimicrobial peptide candidate which has predicted activity against the pathogens involved in respiratory tract infections.
The lead identified here is now undergoing wet-lab validation.
Rising antimicrobial resistance is one of the most pressing global health crises of our time and could result in an estimated 10 million annual deaths globally by 2050.
To prevent this, we urgently need to discover novel therapeutics.

Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), particularly bacteriocins, offer a promising alternative to traditional antibiotics because they have naturally evolved to target fundamental vulnerabilities in competing bacteria, from cell envelopes to essential intracellular machinery, making it difficult for pathogens to develop resistance.
The exponential growth of genomic and metagenomic sequencing has populated global databases with billions of natural amino acid sequences.
This pool of natural data has already produced globally used bacteriocins like Nisin, alongside recent genome-mined breakthroughs such as Darobactin, Dynobactin, and Lariocidin.
Using Google Antigravity allows researchers to navigate the vast biological search space efficiently while leveraging accurate protein function predictions from a domain-specific model.

evidenceRecords.text: Amazon-owned Bee has launched its first new AI devices since its acquisition, including an updated wearable and a credit-card-sized recorder that attaches to smartphones.
The devices can summarize conversations, create to-do lists, and integrate with Alexa and Amazon shopping, with prices starting at $74.99.
Amazon’s personal AI wearable maker, Bee, is announcing its first new products since being acquired by the retail giant last year.

The tech company on Thursday introduced the Bee Frontier, the next generation of its device that can be worn on the wrist or pinned to clothes, along with Bee Eclipse, a credit-card-sized device that magnetically attaches to the back of your smartphone.

The latter puts Bee into more direct competition with AI devices like the Plaud Note or Pocket, but at a lower price point — the Bee Frontier is $74.99, compared with $159 for the Plaud Note (or $189 for the Note Pro), or $129 for the Pocket AI device.

Like the original Bee, the idea with the new devices is to leverage AI to take notes from your everyday conversations, allowing you to remember the important things that were said, and then turn those into actionable to-dos, summaries, and insights.
All Bee devices can create conversation summaries and recaps for free, and offer 14 days of memory.
With an $11.99 per month Bee Pro subscription, users receive unlimited conversation summaries and integrations with Amazon.com, Alexa+, and third-party applications.
Pro users also get suggested to-dos, daily memories, a personal chat assistant, and conversation templates.
To make all this possible, Bee devices use a private computing security architecture, which doesn’t store the raw audio from your conversations.
Instead, audio is processed in real time and then deleted.

Transcripts of the conversation are encrypted using keys that your device creates and controls, which means no one else, including Amazon employees, can access those files unless you manually and intentionally share them.
In addition, you can opt to connect the Bee to Alexa, allowing your Echo device to use its ability to identify your voice, a feature called Voice ID, to recognize when you’re speaking.
It can then record your conversations to provide Bee’s insights. (This aspect of Bee is optional, and Amazon notes you can delete transcripts and summaries at any time.)
With its new connections to Amazon.com and Alexa, Bee users can make purchases from Amazon or ask Alexa for their Bee insights, summaries, or to-dos hands-free.

items.title: AMBA C2C: Moving Forward With A Converged AMBA Foundation For C2C Connectivity
items.originalTitle: AMBA C2C: Moving Forward With A Converged AMBA Foundation For C2C Connectivity
items.summary: In this blog post, we introduce AMBA C2C, a new specification being developed with the AMBA ecosystem. The evolving C2C landscape Chiplet technology and AI are evolving rapidly, bringing new benefits and protocol requirements. AMBA CHI C2C has established strong momentum as a foundational protocol for chiplets and chip-to-chip (C2C) connectivity. AMBA CHI C2C already supports scalability in implementation complexity through a property negotiation mechanism . Many chiplets do not need the full feature set of advanced coherent systems and require an even simpler approach for C2C connectivity.

evidenceRecords.text: In this blog post, we introduce AMBA C2C, a new specification being developed with the AMBA ecosystem.
The evolving C2C landscape Chiplet technology and AI are evolving rapidly, bringing new benefits and protocol requirements.
AMBA CHI C2C has established strong momentum as a foundational protocol for chiplets and chip-to-chip (C2C) connectivity.
AMBA CHI C2C already supports scalability in implementation complexity through a property negotiation mechanism .
Many chiplets do not need the full feature set of advanced coherent systems and require an even simpler approach for C2C connectivity.
This has been an important focus area since we first introduced AMBA CHI C2C in 2023 .
At that time, we discussed how C2C connectivity could extend to simpler, often AXI-based use cases.
Partner feedback since then has reinforced the need for a unified and converged C2C approach for AMBA protocols.
This approach includes both CHI and AXI, rather than separate, protocol-specific point solutions.
Introducing AMBA C2C To address these evolving requirements, we are developing AMBA C2C.
AMBA C2C builds on the success of AMBA CHI C2C.
It provides a converged and scalable C2C foundation across AMBA protocols, including AXI and CHI.

"An element of human psychology that we were drawn to is how cognitive systems can interact depending on the context a person is in.
For example, humans can be quite rational in some situations, yet they act seemingly irrationally in others."
LLMs can approximate and predict human behavior in various ways.
Vitali and Banaji wanted to compare observations of human behavior collected during an earlier study coauthored by Banaji focusing on Bayesian hypocrisy with the reasoning and responses of LLMs.
"Their results showed that people are quite good at this specific probability task.

That is, when participants were asked about whether a man or woman was more likely to be the doctor, and then given new evidence, they combined base rates and evidence much in the way Bayes' rule says they should.
However, the moment a hypothetical 'Other' made that same judgment, they were labeled by those same participants as unfair and inaccurate."

The researchers wanted to understand whether LLMs exhibit the same pattern of Bayesian hypocrisy observed in humans or whether they instead evaluate hypothetical others who make inferences using Bayesian reasoning more favorably.
To do this, they carried out a series of tests with two LLMs, GPT-4o and Claude 3.7 Sonnet.

Thermal co-simulation is the combined simulation of electrical behavior and heat flow across a chip.

In GUC’s thermal integrity design flow, we consider every chip’s power maps and perform thermal crosstalk and dynamic thermal co-simulation to ensure the MCP’s thermal integrity from early-stage through sign-off.
Thermal co-simulation is crucial for GUC’s advanced ASIC workflows.

items.title: Fires Arrive in the Amazon Rainforest
items.originalTitle: Fires Arrive in the Amazon Rainforest
items.summary: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Fires Arrive in the Amazon… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search Unlike a tornado or thunderstorm that can deliver destruction in minutes, El Niño exerts its influence over many months.

evidenceRecords.text: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Fires Arrive in the Amazon… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search Unlike a tornado or thunderstorm that can deliver destruction in minutes, El Niño exerts its influence over many months.

This year, a drought accompanying El Niño has left the Amazon rainforest primed to burn, and scientists say the region has entered the early stages of what they think will be a long and severe fire season.

Starting in September 2026, satellites detected sharp increases in fire activity and smoke emissions in the central and eastern Amazon, visible in fire and emissions monitoring platforms including NASA’s Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS), the Global Fire Emissions Database (GFED), and NASA Worldview .

When the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) on NASA’s Aqua satellite captured this image of smoke streaming from fires on both sides of the Amazon River on October 12, 2026, heavy smoke socked in Manaus, the capital of the Brazilian state of Amazonas.
The pattern begins along the equator with drought and peat fires in Indonesia , followed by elevated fire activity in this part of the Amazon.
“Now, in the Amazon, we’re seeing the second domino in the cascade fall,” Morton said, referring to the uptick in fires that has begun in Pará and Amazonas.
It’s so wet in the Brazilian Amazon that lightning ignites less than 1 percent of fires, so the vast majority of fires currently burning there were started by people, Morton said.

The large fires in this region began as management fires—clearing shrubs from pastures or crops from fields, for instance—but have escaped and are now burning freely through the parched understory of the rainforest, he added.

He plans to share the locations of these “candidate fires” with scientists at MapBiomas , a multi-institutional network comprising universities, NGOs, and technology companies that maps fires and land-use change in the Amazon.

items.originalTitle: Characterization of HBM Power Consumption (ETH Zurich, NYU)
items.summary: Researchers at ETH Zürich and New York University published a technical paper titled “Understanding the Power Consumption of Modern High Bandwidth Memory: Experimental Analysis and Modeling Using Real HBM2 DRAM Chips.” Abstract Excerpt: “We perform the first comprehensive experimental characterization of power consumed by real HBM2 DRAM chips. evidenceRecords.text: Researchers at ETH Zürich and New York University published a technical paper titled “Understanding the Power Consumption of Modern High Bandwidth Memory: Experimental Analysis and Modeling Using Real HBM2 DRAM Chips.” Abstract Excerpt: “We perform the first comprehensive experimental characterization of power consumed by real HBM2 DRAM chips.

Our extensive characterization yields 1) the empirical basis for developing new, accurate HBM power models or validating existing power models and 2) key insights into structural and data-pattern-dependent variation of power in HBM2 chips.

Out of our 13 new findings and 6 key takeaway messages, we highlight: 1) a read operation consumes significantly higher current than any other operation and 2) the toggled data bus signals in a data transfer burst significantly affect current draw where toggling all HBM2-internal bank group bus signals causes 29.4% higher power consumption than keeping them constant.

Leveraging our empirical insights into HBM2 power consumption, we engineer an access pattern that yields 23.6% higher power consumption on average across 36 tested HBM2 chips than the highest-power-consuming JEDEC-specified current measurement loop.” Find the technical paper here .
